(5) Settings never shows an optimistic value: the switches read FabricStatus.settings from the store, which moves only after the node's reply + a GET /fabric refresh (and the fabric frame). The one-time code lives only in the component state that received the reply; an outstanding code after a reload is described, never re-shown.

The host-built `111` binary contains SQLCipher's codec markers (cipher_version + sqlcipher, the same test cross-build.sh applies). I did not run cross-build.sh release builds.
deviations: No cancel route. The contract has no cancel operation, and a cancel route was not in my list of allowed openapi additions. `Fabric::cancel` exists but the API does not reach it, so `reason_code: cancelled` validates against the contract but cannot occur yet. This is recorded in the README §15 as-built note.

Enroll `address` now accepts a host name as well as an IP literal, because the Settings page (U2) sends `host:port`. The route resolves the name once, with a 5 s limit. It dials the first IPv4 answer, falling back to the first answer, because a hub's listener binds 0.0.0.0, which is IPv4 only. The resolved address is what gets stored, not the name, so a hub whose IP changes means enrolling again (v1). A name that does not resolve answers 502 upstream_error. A host whose last label is all digits (e.g. `1.2.3`) is refused with 400, because the system resolver would read it as an old-style IP address.

`POST /fabric/hub/offer` answers 409 bad_request when the node is not a hub (the detail tells the user to turn on the hub role or custody opt-in), and 409 restore_pending when the node has no announce yet, because the offer text needs the card. The contract's offerHub lists only 200 and 403, and I did not add a 409 because that was outside my allowed additions. Suggest the contract add it. The README as-built note now names offer as a restore_pending route.

Listener: when hub_role and listen_lan are both off, nothing listens on 11183, not even on loopback. The contract text for listen_lan says 'otherwise loopback', but spec §2 says loopback is never a peer, so a loopback listener could only refuse everyone. I chose the fail-closed reading.

Quotas: `PATCH /fabric/settings` only accepts the store's refusable classes (kb, update, patch, sync, object, custody); anything else gets 400. The store refuses quotas on human and agent messages (§10.4: messages are never refused). U2's Settings page offers 'msg' and 'agent_op' quota boxes, which will get 400 from the daemon, and it has no boxes for sync, object or custody. That needs a fix on the UI side, in a file I do not own (interface/ui/src/views/settings/messaging-model.ts, QUOTA_CLASSES).

`getThread` with `since_seq`: the store can only return the newest N messages. The route doubles its window up to 4096 rows; past that it answers the oldest page it reached with `more: true`. A `messages_after` query in mesh111 would make this exact.

`Message.at` (display time only): the store keeps no wall clock, so 111d records the first time it sees each message id in `fabric/display-times` (0600, capped at 100k entries). It is never used for ordering or crypto.

Message proposals: the agent's bearer gets 401 for both accepting and dismissing a `kind: message` proposal. The decision file gains an extra field, `applied: {message_id}`, written only after the store commits the message. If writing that file fails, a process-wide guard (keyed by node root and proposal id) stops a retried accept from sending a second time.
The node's own announce carries roles and the home-hub hint as of the last start. A settings change re-mints it at the next start, because the fabric reads its announce once.
Hand-configured direct peers (`peers` in fabric/settings) are set in the file only, not through the API. Their dials are kept open from start.
The `fabric` service row says ERROR 'store could not be opened' even when the real reason is a missing identity; the actual reason is logged once.

Dependencies: the mesh111 path dependency plus `blake2 = "=0.11.0"` as a direct dependency (already in the graph through id111 and mesh111, so no new crates). I checked that every package added to bootstrap/Cargo.lock is at the same version in messaging/Cargo.lock. statvfs uses libc, which node111 already depended on.
Outside the owned list, and allowed by the exception: api_v1/mod.rs gets `pub mod messages/contacts/fabric` and three router merges.
